clue.text: Evidence of trauma or panic mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word for panic is used, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a scare is a sudden panic

explanation.surface: A doctor looking for signs that a patient has suffered shock or fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter from SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the lasting mark left on the body by an injury, visible proof of past harm.

clue.text: Fishy figure not generous about room

indicators.note: about means the word for stingy goes around the abbreviation for room

parts.note: mean means stingy, not generous

explanation.surface: A shady, tight-fisted character who won't make space for anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests suspicious, but it is literal: the figure is half fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A merman is the male counterpart of a mermaid, a mythical creature with a fish's tail.

clue.text: American in nick — new one's arrested? Out of the question

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for American is placed within the word for nick

parts.note: a notch is a nick or small cut

indicators.note: arrested means the word for one holds the abbreviation for new captive inside it

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: An American in a police cell, where a newcomer has been arrested: no hope of escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' looks like British slang for a police station, but it means a cut. Read 'one's arrested' as 'one has arrested' new: ACE holds N to make ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying there is not a chance means something is impossible, wholly out of the question.

clue.text: Quote work held up as lyrical

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A quotation from a work is offered as an example of lyrical writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reverses CITEOP to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing is expressive in the manner of verse, which is what poetic describes.

clue.text: Staunch group of collaborators achieving target of medical research

parts.note: to stem is to staunch, as a flow of blood
a cell is a small group working together, as in a terrorist or political cell

explanation.surface: A loyal team of colleagues reaching their scientific goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' reads as the adjective loyal but is the verb meaning to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem cells, able to develop into other cell types, are a major focus of biomedical study.

clue.text: Grain not left in square

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for left is taken away from the word for grain

parts.note: flour is ground grain

explanation.surface: No grain has been left lying in the town square.
explanation.definitionFit: Four is a square number, being two multiplied by itself.

clue.text: Quiet performer enthralling one in performance

indicators.note: in means the combined piece sits inside the word for performance

parts.note: a turn is a performance, as in a music-hall turn

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the word for performer holds the numeral one

parts.note: an act is a performer or group of performers on a bill
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A silent actor holding someone spellbound on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performer' reads as a person but here is a variety act; 'enthralling' and 'in' are both containment signals, one nested inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says very little, reserved and uncommunicative.

clue.text: Penitent, insincere and damaged, going topless

parts.note: sham means fake or insincere

indicators.note: going topless in a down clue means the word loses its top, first, letter

parts.note: defaced means damaged or disfigured

explanation.surface: Someone sorry, two-faced and broken, who then strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the D from DEFACED, leaving EFACED.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamefaced person shows embarrassment or guilt, much like someone contrite.

clue.text: Leader of church to revise church text

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to redo something is to revise it

explanation.surface: A senior cleric setting out to rewrite a passage of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church' appears twice: its first letter supplies C, and 'church text' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Credo is the Creed, the statement of belief recited in church services.

clue.text: One manipulates commitment to accommodate returning writers

indicators.note: to accommodate means the word for commitment houses the other piece

parts.note: an oath is a solemn commitment

indicators.note: returning means the word for writers is read backwards

parts.note: poets are writers

explanation.surface: A writer who keeps a promise by giving a place to fellow authors coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives STEOP; 'manipulates' looks like scheming, but describes a hands-on therapist.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats patients by manipulating bones and muscles by hand.

clue.text: Shove a lot of rubbish all over the place

parts.note: to ram is to shove forcefully

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: Pushing a mass of litter so it is scattered everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts the final S from PANTS, British slang for something worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rampant spreads unchecked, so it is found everywhere, flourishing wildly.

clue.text: Times is coming in to damage Mirror's lead as leftie stuff

indicators.note: coming in to means these letters enter the combined pieces that follow

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: a word's lead is its first letter

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: One newspaper infiltrating to wreck a rival tabloid's front page with left-wing propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times and the Mirror look like newspapers; here X is the times sign. XIS goes between MAR and the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxism is the political doctrine of Karl Marx, the classic left-wing ideology.

clue.text: Magistrates incline to release daughter with children

indicators.note: to release means the abbreviation for daughter is let go from the word for incline

parts.note: a bend is a curve or incline

explanation.surface: Magistrates inclined to free a girl who has children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incline' looks like a verb meaning to be disposed; it is the noun bend.
explanation.definitionFit: The bench is the collective term for the magistrates or judges sitting in a court.

clue.text: Divinity student swallowing short measure inside bar gets idea

indicators.note: swallowing means the abbreviation for the divinity graduate takes in the rest

parts.note: BD, Bachelor of Divinity, is a graduate in divinity

indicators.note: inside means the short measure goes within the word for bar

parts.note: a rail is a bar
an inch is a short unit of length

explanation.surface: A theology student downing a small drink in a pub comes up with a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short measure' suggests a small drink and 'bar' a pub, but they are a unit of length and a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainchild is an original idea or invention credited to a particular person.

clue.text: Best advertisement for cake

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop
a puff is a promotional piece, a plug

explanation.surface: A baker boasting that this is the finest promotion for a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream puff is a choux pastry filled with whipped cream, a kind of small cake.

clue.text: Devilish chap, very attractive, seen around church, note

parts.note: a chap is a male

indicators.note: seen around means the word for attractive surrounds the following letters

parts.note: fit is British slang for sexually attractive
CE is the Church of England
N is the abbreviation for note, as in footnote references

explanation.surface: A wicked man, handsome and seen near a church, gets noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: FIT is British slang for good-looking; N for note comes from footnote references.
explanation.definitionFit: Maleficent means doing harm or evil, a fitting synonym for wicked or fiendish.

clue.text: Ancient canal lit gaudily in preparation for delivery

indicators.note: gaudily suggests flashy disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old waterway lit up in garish colours, ready for a shipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests goods on a canal, but it means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenatal clinic gives check-ups and classes to expectant mothers before giving birth.

clue.text: Dog second in queue

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail them, follow closely
to second a proposal is to back it

explanation.surface: A dog comes second in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' and 'second' look like nouns but are both verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailback is a long line of stationary traffic backed up along a road.

clue.text: Farewell comment also suppressing lots (but not all)

indicators.note: suppressing means the word for also holds the other piece down inside it

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: but not all means the last letter of the word for lots is dropped

parts.note: oodles means lots, a great deal

explanation.surface: A goodbye remark that also keeps plenty back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not all' leaves OODLE; it sits after the first letter of the word for also.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-oo is a jaunty, old-fashioned British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: The sound of wings?

parts.note: wings suggests birds flapping, but the wings of a theatre are the offstage sides, where sound effects are made

explanation.surface: A question about the noise made by a flapping bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The wings are the sides of a stage, hidden from the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises off are sound effects produced offstage in a theatre, from the wings.

clue.text: Knowing about current manuscript lacking support?

indicators.note: about means the word for knowing goes around the other letters

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing or sharp
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An informed comment on a recent document that has no backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knowing' gives FLY, British slang for streetwise; 'current' is electrical, not recent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy is weak or insubstantial, as if it has nothing holding it up.

clue.text: Married woman at forefront of her country's crime

indicators.note: at forefront of means the word for married woman comes in front of the other piece

parts.note: Frau is German for a married woman, Mrs
D is the international vehicle code for Germany, the Frau's country

explanation.surface: A wife leading the nation's criminal activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her country' is Germany, the home of a Frau, whose car code is D.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is the crime of deceiving people for money or advantage.

clue.text: Historic Royal book featured in urgent announcement

indicators.note: featured in means the abbreviation for book appears inside the word for announcement

parts.note: an alert is an urgent warning

explanation.surface: A book about the royal family covered in a breaking news flash.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert, consort of Queen Victoria, is a famous royal figure from the past.

clue.text: Cooker fix? It's applied at last

parts.note: a hob is the top of a cooker, or a cooker itself
to nail something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: A repair to the stove, finally put into effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' seems to mean finally; a last is a cobbler's foot-shaped model, on which nails go into boot soles.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobnail is a heavy-headed nail hammered into boot soles while the boot sits on a cobbler's form.

clue.text: Old man on a climb, surmounting former peak

indicators.note: surmounting in a down clue means this piece sits on top of the next
on a climb in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, old man
ex means former

explanation.surface: An elderly man climbing above a mountain top he once conquered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a climb' turns PA into AP, placed above EX.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or tip of something, its summit.

clue.text: Oppressive character part of Baden-Powell group? Initially unwanted in that

indicators.note: in means the first letter goes inside the phrase meaning a member of the Cubs, which 'that' points back to

parts.note: Robert Baden-Powell founded the Scouts, whose junior branch is the Cubs; a member is in Cubs

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A bully in the Scouts, plainly unwelcome there.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'part of Baden-Powell group' as IN CUBS, a Cub Scout; 'that' refers back to it, and U goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is an evil spirit that lies on sleepers, so figuratively a burden or oppressive presence.

clue.text: South London suburb falling out of line

parts.note: Kew is a district of southwest London, home of the botanic gardens

explanation.surface: A district of south London is slipping out of step.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is a London suburb famous for its botanic gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Skew means slanting, oblique, not straight or aligned.

clue.text: The French caught idol of Americans womanising

parts.note: le is French for the
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hero is an idol
US, the United States, stands for Americans

explanation.surface: The French catch an American idol chasing women.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecherous man shows excessive sexual desire, as a philanderer does.

clue.text: French writer switching characters shows courage

indicators.note: switching characters means two of the author's letters change places

parts.note: Jules Verne was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A French novelist changing his characters shows bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people in a novel; it means letters. Swap the V and N of VERNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is boldness or daring, the courage to do something risky.
